analysis:
The workflow was supplied as head text only, with no patch, so I could not isolate the changed lines. The CHANGELOG says dev provider releases now default to the dev coordinator, and that prod and local builds keep production defaults. Both env-specific changes bind the environment into the signed binary.

Observed controls in .github/workflows/release-swift.yml:
- build-provider (line 136) sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT from resolve-env.
- The pre-sign smoke (lines 484-485) and the final extracted-artifact smoke (lines 764-765) require 'build-environment-runtime-smoke: ${ENV_PREFIX} '. This catches a resumed or stale unsigned artifact built for the wrong environment (the resume path is at lines 296-301).
- The build-and-release, stage-release and publish-release jobs bind the GitHub environment, so production tags still pass protection rules.
- Secrets are prefixed DEV_/PROD_. The legacy unprefixed fallback applies only to PROD.
- Publication stays separate from qualification: the release key cannot approve builds. The CDHash comes from the final signed artifact (lines 774-780). This is consistent with TB-011, T-054 and A-017.

Open points for the next pass:
- validate-older-macos (lines 1129-1130) does not check the build-environment marker. Low risk, since it is validation-only.
- Signing uses a shared Developer ID and the same bundle ID for dev and prod. A dev-built signed binary has the same team identity as a prod one. I assume exact-CDHash operator qualification (A-017, T-054) is what prevents dev builds being admitted to prod serving, but this was not verified in coordinator code.
- scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh was not supplied, so I could not check that tag pushes force environment=prod and that dispatch cannot mix a prod environment with a dev-built resumed artifact.
- The provider-side default URL logic (Package.swift and ProviderCore) was not supplied.

No concrete regression is established from the supplied text.
